gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
She insisted on ___ for the meal herself.
I'd prefer ___ at home rather than go out tonight.
gaps.explanation: 'Would prefer to do … rather than do'.

gaps.sentence: You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: It's not worth ___ over spilt milk.
The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.

gaps.sentence: I can't stand ___ kept waiting when I have an appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't stand' takes a gerund; the passive gerund is 'being kept'.
